messages:
alex: heads-up — noticed a regression in KV reuse across cross-request prefixes. p95 token latency +18% after yesterday's kernel scheduling change. Repro below.

alex: repro snippet:
```bash
# replay small multi-user longctx workload
for i in $(seq 1 200); do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.local/generate \
    -d '{"prefix":"user:${i%10}:assistant","input":"short convo"}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' &
done
wait
```

kim: thanks — looking now. can you paste the perf flamegraph or the profiler id? :eyes:

perf-bot: flamegraph for run 5381234 (branch/runtime-kernel-4.12): https://perf.internal/fg/5381234 — hot: kv_pager::evict, kv_store::insert, kv_lookup::linear_probe

kim: hmm, eviction spikes line up with the timing of the kernel change we rolled yesterday. suspect fragmentation from non-canonical keys (session suffixes).

maria: we saw this pattern before when session-uuids got appended to the prefix key — duplicates explode kv key_count. quick normalization suggestion: drop ephemeral suffixes before hashing. e.g.:
```py
def canonicalize_prefix(prefix):
    # strip ephemeral session uuids e.g. /s/<uuid>
    return re.sub(r"/s/[0-9a-f-]{8,}", "", prefix)
```

josh: can repro locally on my dev box with the longctx harness. memory climbs then pager enters tight loop -> thrash. logs look like repeated inserts for same logical prefix but slightly different bytes.

alex: sample log lines from my run:
```
[22:03:10] kv.insert key=tenantA:user:1234/prompt_v2
[22:03:10] kv.insert key=tenantA:user:1234/prompt_v2/s/8f3a7c
[22:03:10] kv.insert key=tenantA:user:1234/prompt_v2/s/9c1d4b
[22:03:11] kv.evict victim=0x7f9a... recycled=12
```

josh: propose short-term mitigations: (1) add a key-normalize pass in the insert path (cheap), (2) add an in-memory dedupe bloom before write, (3) metric kv.insert.dup_rate so we can alert when duplication > threshold.

kim: agree, but also want to check batching heuristics impact — larger batches change arrival patterns so prefix locality drops and fragmentation rises. kernel scheduling tweak might have changed micro-batching alignment. we should measure prefix locality vs batch size.

maria: short-term routing option: enable session-affinity for cache (route same prefix to same worker/GPU) to increase reuse while we fix keying. config idea: `cache.session_affinity: true` with hash(window_ms=1000).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back runtime-kernel-4.12 on eng-runtime-prod @ 2026-03-17T22:10Z :arrow_backward:

alex: nice rollback. i'll open a tiny PR with key-normalize + unit tests + a replay harness for the longctx scenario. will include kv.insert.dup_rate metric.

josh: i'll attach a minimal reproducer and the flamegraphs to the ticket. pinging @kim to run bisect on kernel changes vs batch alignments.

kim: thanks — i'll bisect and run a short job that emits `kv.key_count` and `kv.unique_logical_keys` per minute. if unique_logical_keys / key_count < 0.85 then we have high duplication and it's a keying problem.

maria: :+1: once we have metrics we can set an alert and a canary with dedupe enabled.

alex: cool. priority: 1) key-normalize + metric, 2) canary dedupe, 3) evaluate session_affinity routing. thanks everyone.
